general_background.title: Conversion of a precursor
general_background.summary: Thermal decomposition changes a precursor into species available for further reaction or growth. Bond cleavage and ligand transformations can change the supply of growth species, with competing pathways set by the precursor and medium.

general_background.title: Carboxylic-acid and carboxylate ligands
general_background.summary: Carboxylic acids and carboxylates can associate with metal-containing surfaces and solution species through their oxygen groups. The hydrocarbon part of a long-chain ligand can favour dispersion in a compatible solvent, while acid-base equilibria influence how its head group associates.

general_background.title: Phosphine-oxide coordination
general_background.summary: A phosphine oxide can interact with suitable precursor or surface sites through its oxygen donor. Competition among oxygen-donor ligands can change precursor coordination and the availability of surface sites.
